questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How loud music damages young people's ears
How the ear works and why hearing gets worse with age
The best hearing aids available in the UK
Why some people hear better than others at birth
questions.why: They explain how the ear works and discover why we lose hearing as we get older.

questions.q: What does Neil say about his own hearing?
options: He has used a hearing aid for years
He often asks people to speak more loudly
He lost some of his hearing after years of working with loud machines
He worried about it once, but a check-up showed it was fine
questions.why: Neil thought his ears might be getting worse, but a check-up showed everything was fine.

questions.q: What does Georgie say about hearing loss in the UK?
options: It affects 18 million people and is increasing
It affects about 18 million people, but the number is falling
It mostly affects people over 80
It affects about one person in eight
questions.why: She says hearing loss affects 18 million people in the UK and that number is increasing.

questions.q: Why does surgeon Nish Mehta compare the outer ear to a satellite dish?
options: Because it makes sounds much louder
Because it sends signals to the brain
Because it collects sounds and directs them inwards
Because it is the most delicate and easily damaged part of the ear
questions.why: He says the pinna 'collects the sounds' and funnels them towards the sense organ.

questions.q: According to Nish Mehta, when does wear and tear of our hearing begin?
options: At birth
In our forties
At around eight years old
When we reach retirement age
questions.why: He says wear and tear of hearing starts from around the age of eight.

questions.q: Why does Nish Mehta mention someone who uses a pneumatic drill?
options: To show that noise can speed up hearing loss, even with good genes
To explain why builders need regular ear operations
To show that the genes you are born with matter far more than noise
To give an example of a sound that can't be heard
questions.why: He says someone with strong genetics who spends life on a drill may decline faster.

questions.q: Why do people often take a long time to notice their hearing is getting worse?
options: Because hearing loss has no effect on speech
Because the outer ears grow bigger with age to catch more sound
Because doctors rarely test adults' hearing
Because the brain works harder to make up for it
questions.why: Nish says the brain increases its listening effort, so it's slow to realise you're struggling.

questions.q: Which way of helping hearing loss is NOT mentioned?
options: Hearing aids
Taking special vitamins
Surgery
Removing extra ear wax from the ears
questions.why: Georgie mentions hearing aids, surgery and removing ear wax, but nothing about vitamins.
